5º de Primaria · Inglés

Past simple of to be: was and were

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

En inglés, «estoy cansado» es I am tired. ¿Y cómo dirías «ayer estaba cansado»?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Diciendo Yesterday I was tired. El verbo to be (ser o estar) tiene en pasado solo dos formas: was y were. Con ellas puedes contar dónde estabas, cómo te sentías o cómo era algo: «It was sunny», «We were at the beach».

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: Grandma's old school

Last Sunday, Lucas visited his grandma Carmen. She showed him an old black-and-white photo.

«This was my school in 1965,» she said. «I was ten years old, like you.»

Lucas looked at the photo carefully. «Where were the computers, Grandma?»

Grandma laughed. «There weren't any computers! There was a big blackboard and there were forty children in my class. The desks were made of wood and there was a little hole for the ink.»

«Forty children? Was it noisy?»

«No, it wasn't! Our teacher, Don Julián, was very strict. But he was also very kind. His stories about the stars were fantastic.»

«Were you a good student?» asked Lucas with a smile.

«I was good at Maths, but my handwriting was terrible,» she answered.

On Monday, Lucas told his class about Grandma's school. Everybody was surprised. Life in the past was very different!

(En esta lectura aparecen was, were y sus negativas. Fíjate también en there was y there were: significan «había».)

1. From present to past

You already know the verb to be in the present: I am, you are, he is, we are. When we talk about the past, these forms change. Am and is become was. Are becomes were. That's all!

«Today I am at school. Yesterday I was at home.» «Now they are happy. Last week they were sad.» En castellano: was y were sirven para «era», «estaba», «fue» o «estuvo». El inglés usa la misma palabra para ser y para estar, así que es más fácil que en español.

2. Was or were?

Use was with I, he, she and it (one person or thing). Use were with you, we and they. Remember: you always takes were, even when you talk to only one friend: «You were great in the match, Lucía!»

With names and nouns, think: one or more than one? «My dog was hungry.» «My dogs were hungry.» «Marta was in the library.» «Marta and Pau were in the park.» Truco: si puedes cambiarlo por he, she o it, usa was; si es they, usa were.

Vídeo: Was – Were: past simple, verb to be for kids · Interesting English (YouTube) · 426 mil visualizaciones

3. There was and there were

You already know there is and there are (hay). In the past, they become there was and there were. In Spanish, both mean «había».

  • Use there was with one thing (singular) or with uncountable nouns: «There was a cat in the garden.» «There was some milk in the fridge.»
  • Use there were with two or more things (plural): «There were three cats in the garden.» «There were lots of people at the concert.»

Negatives: there wasn't / there weren't. We often use any in negative sentences: «There wasn't a TV.» «There weren't any computers.»

Questions: change the order. «Was there a park near your house?» – «Yes, there was.» / «No, there wasn't.» «Were there many children?» – «Yes, there were.»

Careful! In Spanish we say «había un gato» and «había tres gatos» with the same word. In English, you must choose was or were depending on what comes next.

Vídeo: Usando los verbos Be Was y Were correctamente · Tiny Teaching Tube (YouTube) · 75 mil visualizaciones

4. Time words for the past

When we use was and were, we often say when. These are useful time expressions: yesterday (ayer), yesterday morning, last night (anoche), last week, last month, last year, last summer, two days ago (hace dos días), in 2020.

They can go at the beginning or at the end of the sentence: «Last Sunday we were at my grandma's house» or «We were at my grandma's house last Sunday». Ojo: decimos last night, no the last night, y ago va siempre detrás: three years ago.

5. I was born in…

To talk about birthdays and the place where someone started their life, English uses was born / were born. In Spanish it means «nací», «nació», «nacieron».

  • «I was born in 2015.» (Nací en 2015.)
  • «My brother was born in Valencia.»
  • «My cousins were born in the same hospital.»
  • «When were you born?» – «I was born on 12th May.»
  • «Where was your mum born?» – «She was born in Lima, in Peru.»

Remember the prepositions: in + year, month or city (in 2015, in May, in Seville); on + a date or a day (on 12th May, on Monday).

We also use was born to talk about famous people in history:

  • «Miguel de Cervantes was born in Alcalá de Henares in 1547.»
  • «Marie Curie was born in Warsaw, in Poland, in 1867. She was a famous scientist.»
  • «Pablo Picasso was born in Málaga in 1881. He was a painter.»

Never say «I born» or «I am born». The correct form is always I was born.

6. Negatives: wasn't and weren't

To make a negative, add not after was or were. In speaking and in informal writing we join them: was not → wasn't and were not → weren't. «I wasn't at the party.» «The shops weren't open.»

We don't need did or don't with the verb to be. Never say «I didn't was». Pronunciación: wasn't suena «uósnt» y weren't, «uérnt». Practise with true sentences about yesterday: «I wasn't late for school. My friends weren't in the playground at eight.»

7. Questions: Was it…? Were you…?

To ask a question, we change the order: Was or Were goes first, then the subject. «You were tired» → «Were you tired?» «It was cold» → «Was it cold?»

Short answers repeat was or were: «Yes, I was.» «No, I wasn't.» «Yes, they were.» «No, it wasn't.» In short answers we never say «Yes, I was tired» with all the words… we can, but it is more natural to stop after was. En castellano: en inglés no basta con la entonación; hay que cambiar el orden de las palabras.

8. Wh- questions

We can start with a question word: Where, When, Who, What, How, Why. The order is: question word + was/were + subject. «Where were you yesterday?» «I was at the swimming pool.» «How was the trip?» «It was amazing!»

«Who was your first teacher?» «What was the weather like?» «Why were you late?» «Because the bus was slow.» Consejo: How was…? es la pregunta perfecta para el lunes: «How was your weekend?».

9. Describing the past

With was and were we can describe people, places and things in the past. Feelings: «I was nervous / excited / bored.» Weather: «It was windy / rainy / foggy.» Places: «The beach was crowded.» People: «My grandparents were very young in this photo.»

We also use there was (one thing) and there were (more than one) to say what existed: «There was a big castle on the hill. There were lots of tourists.» En castellano: there was / there were es «había».

10. Then and now

We can use was and were to compare the past with the present. Look at the time words: in the past, fifty years ago, when I was little; and now, today, nowadays.

  • «Fifty years ago, phones were big and heavy. Now they are small and light.»
  • «In the past, there were no computers in schools. Today there are computers in every classroom.»
  • «When I was little, my favourite toy was a teddy bear. Now it is my bike.»
  • «My dad was shy at school, but now he is a teacher!»

To describe the change, we often use but: «The village was quiet, but now it is busy.»

You can also use comparatives: «The streets were darker. Cars were slower.»

This is a great way to learn about history. Ask your grandparents: «What was your town like? Where were the shops? Was there a cinema?» Their answers are a window to the past.

11. Reading: a day at the museum

Read Pablo's text: «Last Friday my class was at the Science Museum. The bus was very early, at eight o'clock, so we were a bit sleepy. The museum was enormous. There were dinosaur bones and a planetarium. My favourite room was the space room. The guide was funny and the experiments were fantastic. The café wasn't open, but our sandwiches were delicious. It was a great day!»

Answer: Where was the class? Why were they sleepy? Was the café open? What was Pablo's favourite room?

12. Let's practise: my old photo

Bring a photo from when you were little, or draw one. Write five sentences: «In this photo I was three years old. I was at the park with my mum. My hair was very short. It was summer. There were ducks in the lake.»

Then play in pairs: your partner asks questions to guess the details. «Were you happy?» «Was it your birthday?» «Who was with you?» Repaso final: I, he, she, it → was; you, we, they → were; negativa con n't; pregunta cambiando el orden.

13. Pronunciation: was and were

Listen to native speakers and you will notice something interesting: was and were sound different in different positions.

  • In the middle of a sentence, they are usually weak (débiles) and short: «I was at home» sounds like /ai wəz at hoom/. «They were happy» sounds like /dei wə hapi/.
  • At the end of a short answer or when we want to stress them, they are strong: «Yes, I was!» sounds like /woz/. «Yes, they were!» sounds like /wer/ (in British English, almost /wə:/).
  • The negatives wasn't /wóznt/ and weren't /wernt/ are always strong.

Don't pronounce the letter w like a Spanish «gu» too strongly: put your lips in a circle, like for the sound «u», and then open them.

Practise with this chant, clapping on the strong words:

«Where were you? I was at school.
Where was Tom? He was at the pool.
Were you tired? Yes, I was!
Was it cold? No, it wasn't!»

Saying chants aloud is a fun way to remember grammar and to improve your rhythm in English.

14. Writing: a short biography

A biography is a text about a person's life. With was, were and was born you can write a short one. Follow these steps:

  1. Choose a person: a famous person, or someone in your family (your grandmother, your uncle…).
  2. Find information: when and where was he or she born? What was his or her job? What was special about this person?
  3. Organise the text in three paragraphs:
    • Birth and childhood: «Gloria Fuertes was born in Madrid in 1917. Her family was poor.»
    • Life and work: «She was a poet. Her poems were for children. They were funny and full of animals.»
    • Why he or she is important: «She was very popular on TV. Her books are still famous today.»
  4. Check: was with I, he, she, it; were with you, we, they. Use capital letters for names, cities and countries.

Add a photo or a drawing and a title. Then read your biography to the class. Your classmates can ask questions: «Was she married? Were her books expensive?»

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Complete with was or were: «My sister ___ ill and my parents ___ worried.»

  1. My sister = she (una persona) → was.
  2. My parents = they (varias) → were.

Resultado: My sister was ill and my parents were worried.

Ejemplo 2. Make it negative: «The film was scary.»

  1. Con to be no usamos didn't.
  2. was + not = wasn't.

Resultado: The film wasn't scary.

Ejemplo 3. Make a question and answer it: «You were at home last night.» (yes)

  1. Cambiamos el orden: Were + you…?
  2. Respuesta corta: Yes, I was.

Resultado: Were you at home last night? Yes, I was.

Ejemplo 4. Complete with there was or there were: «___ a big tree in the square and ___ two benches.»

  1. A big tree = one thing → there was.
  2. Two benches = plural → there were.

Resultado: There was a big tree in the square and there were two benches.

Ejemplo 5. Write a question and answer: you / born / 2015? (yes)

  1. Question with be: Were + you + born…?
  2. Short answer with was: Yes, I was.

Resultado: Were you born in 2015? Yes, I was.

Errores típicos

  • Usar was con you: «You was late» → «You were late».
  • Usar did con to be: «I didn't was» → «I wasn't»; «Did you were…?» → «Were you…?».
  • No cambiar el orden en la pregunta: «You were tired?» → «Were you tired?».
  • Decir «the last night» o «ago two days» → «last night», «two days ago».
  • Responder solo «Yes» o «No» sin was/were: mejor «Yes, I was» / «No, I wasn't».
  • Decir «I born in 2015» o «I am born»: la forma correcta es «I was born in 2015».
  • Usar there was con plural: «There was three cats» → «There were three cats».

Ejercicios (25)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Complete: «There ___ a dog in the park. There ___ two children.»

    Ver solución
    was, were.

  2. Translate: «Nací en Sevilla.»

    Ver solución
    I was born in Seville.

  3. Make it negative: «There were computers in the classroom.»

    Ver solución
    There weren't any computers in the classroom.

  4. Write the question: «There was a cinema in your town.»

    Ver solución
    Was there a cinema in your town?

  5. Complete with in or on: «I was born ___ 2014, ___ 3rd June.»

    Ver solución
    in, on.

Nivel medio

  1. Complete: «I ___ at home. You ___ at school.»

    Ver solución
    was, were.

  2. Complete: «The cats ___ in the garden.»

    Ver solución
    were (the cats = they).

  3. Change to the past: «It is hot today.» (yesterday)

    Ver solución
    It was hot yesterday.

  4. Make it negative: «We were in Madrid.»

    Ver solución
    We weren't in Madrid.

  5. Make a question: «Your teacher was happy.»

    Ver solución
    Was your teacher happy?

  6. Answer with a short answer: «Were they at the party?» (no)

    Ver solución
    No, they weren't.

  7. Order the words: «you / where / yesterday / were / ?»

    Ver solución
    Where were you yesterday?

  8. Correct the mistake: «My friends was very kind.»

    Ver solución
    My friends were very kind.

  9. Translate: «Anoche había una luna enorme.»

    Ver solución
    Last night there was an enormous moon.

  10. Write three sentences about your last birthday with was and were.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I was ten. My friends were at my house. The cake was chocolate.

  11. Write three sentences about your bedroom when you were little: there was / there were.

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: There was a small bed. There were lots of toys.

  12. Answer: «When were you born? Where were you born?»

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: I was born on 5th March 2015. I was born in Bilbao.

  13. Write two sentences comparing then and now: phones, schools or toys.

    Ver solución
    Example: Phones were big. Now they are small.

  14. Correct: «Picasso born in Málaga and he were a painter.»

    Ver solución
    Picasso was born in Málaga and he was a painter.

  15. Complete the chant: «Where ___ you? I ___ at school.»

    Ver solución
    were, was.

  16. Is was weak or strong here? «Yes, I was!» / «I was at home.»

    Ver solución
    Strong in «Yes, I was!»; weak in «I was at home».

Nivel avanzado

  1. Interview an older person and write five sentences about his or her school.

    Ver solución
    Open answer with was, were, there was and there were.

  2. Write a short biography of a famous person in three paragraphs.

    Ver solución
    Open answer: birth, life and work, why important.

  3. Write five questions to ask your grandparents about the past.

    Ver solución
    Example: Was there a cinema? Were the streets busy? Where were you born?

  4. Describe a photo of your town fifty years ago and today.

    Ver solución
    Open answer comparing was/were and is/are.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeOur town in the past

La clase prepara una exposición en inglés sobre cómo era su pueblo o barrio en el pasado, con entrevistas a personas mayores.

Pasos

  1. Prepare five questions in English with was, were, there was and there were.
  2. Interview a grandparent or an older neighbour (en castellano si hace falta) and take notes.
  3. Write a short text «Our town in the past» comparing then and now, with photos.
  4. Present your poster to the class and answer your classmates' questions.

Producto final: Una exposición de carteles «Then and now» con entrevistas y fotos.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses was and were correctly with each person.
  • Uses there was / there were.
  • Talks about birth with was born.
  • Compares the past and the present.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • A la hora de cenar, preguntad «How was your day?» y que responda con dos frases con was o were.
  • Mirad fotos antiguas de la familia y describidlas en inglés: «Grandma was young. We were at the beach».
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Expresión de hechos y estados en el pasado; verbo to be en pasado: afirmativa, negativa e interrogativa (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Álbum de fotos de la infancia con frases en pasado.
  • Juego «Where were you?»: cada alumno inventa dónde estaba ayer a una hora y los demás preguntan.
  • Mímica de emociones: «You were angry!».

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Use was and were to talk about the past (hablar del pasado)
  • Choose was or were for each person
  • Make negatives with wasn't and weren't
  • Ask and answer questions: Was it…? Were you…?
  • Use there was and there were (había)
  • Talk about birthdays and history with was born
  • Compare the past and the present and write a short biography

Palabras clave

to be · was · were · wasn't · weren't · Was…? · Were…? · yesterday · last night · ago

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
